prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Swimming kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the COMPETITION SWIMSUIT — one single garment, a racerback one-piece that covers the torso and fastens between the legs, laid flat and face up, with high-cut leg openings and a plain closed back. There is NO separate shirt, NO separate shorts and NO separate top
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the SILICONE SWIM CAP laid flat with its dome up, and the GOGGLES laid beside it with both lenses face up and the strap open — each its own separate item, never on top of another garment

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A ROYAL BLUE ONE-PIECE COMPETITION SWIMSUIT exactly as photo2.png shows it, and it is the WHOLE uniform — one single garment covering the torso and fastening between the legs. A plain round SCOOP NECKLINE, THIN shoulder straps, and legs cut HIGH at the hip. The body of it is PLAIN ROYAL BLUE all over: there is NO contrasting stripe down the sides, no panel and no trim of any other colour, whatever the sport default says. The club badge sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST, printed in WHITE — the bayline-marlins mark with its ARCH outline (flat base, semicircular top) drawn as a narrow band with the marlin inside it, about a palm across. It is the ONLY mark on the suit. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering anywhere. The BACK of the suit is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it is a PLAIN CLOSED BACK in the same royal blue — no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Swimming does not number a racing suit, and a number printed across her back would be a mark this suit does not have.
- shorts: There is NO separate lower garment of any kind: no shorts, no jammers, no tights, no briefs under the suit. The one-piece racing suit IS the whole uniform, and her LEGS ARE BARE from the high-cut hip to the floor, exactly as photo2.png shows her on the pool deck.
- socks: NO SOCKS. Swimming is competed barefoot and no sock appears in any photograph. Her feet and ankles are bare in every frame.
- footwear: BARE FEET. No shoes, no sandals, no pool slides of any kind — she stands and walks on the wet deck barefoot, exactly as photo2.png shows. Do not put footwear on her in any frame.
- equipment: TWO ITEMS BELONG TO THE KIT, and they are worn to SWIM rather than all day: a plain ROYAL BLUE SILICONE SWIM CAP, smooth and completely unmarked — no maker's logo, no lettering, no club name — covering the whole head with the hairline showing at the front, and GOGGLES with dark MIRRORED lenses in a soft silver-grey on plain dark straps, also unbranded. photo2.png shows both at the pool, the goggles hanging around her NECK, which is where they sit when she is not actually swimming; photo3.png shows the goggles on at the wall. In photo1.png and photo4.png, away from the pool, she wears neither — they are kit, not part of her. She also carries a plain unbranded MESH KIT BAG on one shoulder in photo2.png, on the way out. The DECISION for the poses is that the cap and goggles are ON in every frame and the bag is NOT: no kit bag, no kickboard, no float, no paddles and no towel in her hands.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST of the swimsuit, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not shrink it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST of the swimsuit, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not shrink it and do not add a second mark beside it. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
